clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work; his wife Celeste left him in August; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton; and your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. Your grandmother's functioning came back when she took a job at the library in May 1979, and the shifts settle there.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984–1985
clusters.reason: Around your mother being ordered to bed for pregnancy in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with her over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and you would not sleep unless your father sat by the bed. Your sister Ines was born in September 1984, and the shifts settle in the months after.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's disease, 1986–1997
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis of Parkinson's disease in September 1986, within the years: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news; Hazel had a bad fall in 1988 and her functioning fell; your father and uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather had chest pains; Hazel's functioning fell again and she could not dress herself; your mother overfunctioned taking her to the clinic; your father drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel; your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left Hazel's side; and your father and mother fought over his evenings at his parents' house. Hazel moved to the Fairlie nursing home in June 1997, and your father cut his drinking back to weekends in October, where the shifts settle.

clusters.name: Callum leaving for the north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for a job at the mines in May 1999: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother's anxiety rose at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage, his functioning down; your sister Ines skipped school through the autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere; and Ines's functioning came back when she returned to school full days and passed her exams in August 2000, and the shifts settle there.
